pr_body:
Support to timezone types on Pandas.

Note that similarly to Arrow, the timezones are stored in DuckDB in UTC, and will follow the mask value set in the database.

Fix: #4267
pr_comments: @Mause feel free to nitpick, I've mostly wroten python code for config/experiment scripts, so your comments are very welcome.
@Tishj I did a lot of refactoring regarding the ```PandasTypes```  could you please check if these still make sense and work as they were supposed to work?

LGTM!

Definitely much cleaner, only things I can think of is that the numpy dtypes were the full list of dtypes that numpy uses, so they might show up as edge cases later.
But we weren't converting to them anyways, so it's better to remove them than to leave them uncovered.

The removal of ColumnIsMasked had me scratching my head, but it looks like the "mask" attribute check I added obsoleted the other checks, which I didn't catch at the time 😅

issue_context.title: duckdb to/from pandas does not preserve timezone awareness
issue_context.body:
### What happens?

duckdb preserves timezone-awareness during to/from arrow conversion, but the same information is lost when converting to/from pandas.



### To Reproduce


```python
# Create pandas DataFrame with timezone-aware timestamp column and corresponding arrow table:
import duckdb
import pandas as pd
import pyarrow as pa

df = pd.DataFrame(
    {"timestamp": [pd.Timestamp("2022-01-01", tz="America/New_York")]}
)
arrow_table = pa.Table.from_pandas(df)

con = duckdb.connect()

# duckdb to/from arrow preserves timezone awareness:
con.execute("DESCRIBE (SELECT * FROM arrow_table)").fetchall()
# Output:
# [('timestamp', 'TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE', 'YES', None, None, None)]
con.execute("SELECT * from arrow_table").fetch_arrow_table()
# Output:
# pyarrow.Table
# timestamp: timestamp[us, tz=UTC]
# ----
# timestamp: [[2022-01-01 05:00:00.000000]]

# duckdb to/from pandas drops timezone awareness:
con.execute("DESCRIBE (SELECT * FROM df)").fetchall()
# Output:
# [('timestamp', 'TIMESTAMP', 'YES', None, None, None)]
con.execute("SELECT * from arrow_table").df().dtypes
# Output:
# timestamp    datetime64[ns]
# dtype: object
```



### OS:

OSX

### DuckDB Version:

0.4.1.dev1115 (and 0.4.0)

### DuckDB Client:

Python

### Full Name:

Erin Ovechkin

None
